meta.description: Export complete customer, account, card, cross-reference, and transaction data from the CardDemo system into a structured migration file to support branch migration initiatives.
meta.process_description: CBEXPORT is a batch data migration program that reads all normalised CardDemo source files sequentially and consolidates them into a single multi-record-type export file, where each record is tagged with a type indicator (C=Customer, A=Account, etc.) along with a branch identifier, region code, and timestamp. The program processes each data domain in turn — customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, and cards — writing one export record per source record in a fixed 500-character format with a unique sequence number. Throughout processing, the program accumulates per-entity and total export counts, which are reported at completion to provide an audit trail of the migration run. The output file is intended for consumption by a receiving system (e.g. a new branch platform), with the companion program CBIMPORT likely performing the corresponding load operation at the destination.

files.CUSTFILE: Source file of customer demographic and identity records (names, addresses, SSN, FICO scores, contact details)
files.ACCTFILE: Source file of credit card account records (balances, credit limits, status, dates)
files.XREFFILE: Source cross-reference file linking card numbers to customer and account identifiers
files.TRANSACT: Source file of credit card transaction records for the accounts being migrated
files.CARDFILE: Source file of physical credit card records associated with accounts
files.EXPFILE: Output migration export file containing all record types in a unified 500-character fixed-format structure, keyed by sequence number

business_rules: All five source data domains (customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, cards) must be successfully opened before any export processing begins; failure to open any file causes immediate program termination.
Every exported record is stamped with the branch ID '0001' and region code 'NORTH', indicating this export is scoped to a specific branch migration event and is not a generic full-system export.

Each export record receives a globally unique, monotonically increasing sequence number across all record types, enabling the receiving system to detect gaps, duplicates, or ordering issues during import.

Sensitive customer identity data — including Social Security Number (SSN), government-issued ID, date of birth, and FICO credit score — is exported in full without masking, requiring strict access controls on the export file.
Any I/O error during reading of source files or writing of the export file causes immediate abnormal program termination (ABEND), ensuring no partial or corrupt migration file is silently accepted.

The export processes each entity type as a complete, independent pass through its source file (sequential full-file reads), meaning the export captures a point-in-time snapshot per entity type rather than a single consistent snapshot across all entities simultaneously.

Export statistics (record counts per entity type and total) are displayed at job completion, providing an operational audit record for reconciliation against the import counts in the receiving system.

lines.explanation: This is the master orchestration paragraph that drives the entire branch migration export run. It sequences every phase of the migration — from setup through data extraction of all five business domains to final reporting — ensuring a complete, ordered export of all customer, account, card, and transaction data into the migration file.
Initialises the export run: opens all source and output files, captures the run timestamp, and prepares counters and sequence numbering before any data is processed.
Performs a full sequential pass through all customer demographic and identity records, writing each customer to the migration export file with a record type tag and sequence number.
Performs a full sequential pass through all credit card account records — including balances, credit limits, and status — writing each account to the migration export file.
Performs a full sequential pass through all card-to-customer-to-account cross-reference linkage records, writing each relationship mapping to the migration export file.
Performs a full sequential pass through all credit card transaction history records associated with the migrating accounts, writing each transaction to the migration export file.
Performs a full sequential pass through all physical credit card records tied to the migrating accounts, writing each card record to the migration export file.
Finalises the migration run: closes all files, tallies the total records exported across all five business domains, and displays the per-entity and overall export counts for audit and reconciliation.
Returns control to the operating system, signalling the successful completion of the batch migration export job.

This paragraph performs all pre-processing setup required before the migration export can begin, capturing the exact date and time of the run and ensuring all source and destination files are ready for processing. It establishes the operational context for the entire migration job and provides an auditable start marker in the job log.

Entry point for the timestamp generation routine, called once at the start of the export run.
Reads the current calendar date from the operating system in four-digit-year format to ensure year-2000-compliant date recording.
Reads the current time of day from the operating system, capturing hours, minutes, seconds, and hundredths for precise run identification.
Assembles the date components into the internationally recognised YYYY-MM-DD format, making the export date unambiguous across regional date conventions.
Stores the formatted calendar date into the working date field that will later be combined into the full export timestamp.
Assembles the time components into HH:MM:SS format, providing a human-readable and system-parseable representation of the exact time of the export run.
Stores the formatted time of day into the working time field ready for inclusion in the final timestamp.
Combines the formatted date, a space separator, the formatted time, and a fractional-seconds suffix to produce the complete 26-character timestamp applied to every record in the migration file.

Stores the fully assembled date-and-time stamp into the field that will be written onto each exported record, ensuring every customer, account, card, cross-reference, and transaction record carries an identical run timestamp for traceability.

Outputs the total number of credit card transaction history records successfully written to the export file.
Outputs the total number of physical card records successfully written to the export file.
Begins writing the overall record count to the job log as the final reconciliation figure.
Outputs the cumulative count of all records written across every entity type, providing the single reconciliation total that the receiving branch system must match upon import.
Entry point invoked whenever a fatal, unrecoverable error is detected anywhere during the migration export process.
Writes a clear diagnostic message to the job log, alerting operations staff that the migration export has failed and terminated abnormally rather than completing successfully.

Triggers a controlled abnormal termination of the migration job, producing a non-zero return code so that downstream job scheduling and operations monitoring systems can detect the failure and prevent the incomplete export file from being passed to the receiving branch platform.

variables.name: EXPORT-OUTPUT-RECORD
variables.description: The physical 500-character output buffer that holds a fully assembled export record at the moment it is written to the migration file. Every entity type (customer, account, card, cross-reference, transaction) is formatted into this single fixed-length slot before being flushed to disk, ensuring the receiving branch system always reads uniform-length records regardless of the underlying data type.

variables.name: WS-FILE-STATUS-AREA
variables.description: A grouped control area that tracks the health of every file involved in the migration export — five source files and the output export file. After every read or write operation the operating system posts a two-character status code here, allowing the program to detect end-of-file, successful I/O, or errors and react accordingly (e.g., abort on error, stop reading at end-of-file).

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-STATUS
variables.description: The I/O status code returned by the operating system after each read operation against the Customer source file (CUSTFILE). The program inspects this code to determine whether the last customer record was read successfully, whether all customer records have been exhausted, or whether a file error has occurred that would compromise the integrity of the migration.

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-EOF
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the program has read the very last customer record from CUSTFILE (status code '10' = end-of-file). When this condition is true, the customer export pass is complete and no more customer records remain to be migrated.

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-OK
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the most recent read of the Customer source file completed without any error (status code '00' = success). The program uses this to confirm that a valid customer record was retrieved and is safe to format and export.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-STATUS
variables.description: The I/O status code returned after each read operation against the Account source file (ACCTFILE). The program checks this to confirm whether a credit card account record was read successfully, whether all accounts have been processed, or whether a file error has occurred that would require immediate termination of the export.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-EOF
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the program has read the last account record from ACCTFILE. When true, the account export pass is finished and all credit card account data has been written to the migration file.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-OK
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the most recent read of the Account source file succeeded without error. The program uses this to confirm that a valid account record (with balances, credit limits, and status) is in memory and ready to be exported.

variables.name: WS-XREF-STATUS
variables.description: The I/O status code returned after each read of the Card Cross-Reference file (XREFFILE), which links card numbers to their owning customer and account. This status tells the program whether the linkage record was read cleanly, whether all cross-references have been exported, or whether a file error has disrupted the relationship mapping.

variables.name: WS-XREF-EOF
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the last card-to-account cross-reference record has been read from XREFFILE. When true, all card-customer-account linkage data has been captured in the migration file and the cross-reference export pass is complete.

variables.name: WS-XREF-OK
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the most recent read of the Cross-Reference file succeeded. The program uses this to confirm that a valid card-to-customer-to-account linkage record is available and can be safely written to the export file.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACTION-STATUS
variables.description: The I/O status code returned after each read of the Transaction source file (TRANSACT). This status allows the program to determine whether a transaction record (purchase, payment, cash advance, etc.) was read successfully, whether all transactions have been exported, or whether a file error has occurred that would leave the transaction history incomplete in the migration file.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACTION-EOF
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the last transaction record has been read from TRANSACT. When true, the full transaction history for the migrating accounts has been written to the export file and the transaction export pass is complete.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACTION-OK
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the most recent read of the Transaction file succeeded without error. The program uses this to confirm that a valid transaction record is in memory and ready to be stamped with the migration metadata and written to the export file.

variables.name: WS-CARD-STATUS
variables.description: The I/O status code returned after each read of the Card source file (CARDFILE), which holds physical card details such as card number, CVV, embossed name, and expiry date. This status tells the program whether the card record was retrieved successfully, whether all cards have been processed, or whether a file error has occurred.

variables.name: WS-CARD-EOF
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the last physical card record has been read from CARDFILE. When true, all card data (including card numbers, CVV codes, and expiry dates) has been written to the migration file and the card export pass is complete.

variables.name: WS-CARD-OK
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the most recent read of the Card file succeeded without error. The program uses this to confirm that a valid physical card record is in memory and safe to export to the migration file.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-STATUS
variables.description: The I/O status code returned by the operating system after each write operation to the output migration export file (EXPFILE). The program checks this after every record write to confirm the data was successfully persisted; any non-zero status triggers an immediate abnormal termination to prevent a silently corrupt or incomplete migration file from being delivered to the receiving branch.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-OK
variables.description: A named business condition that evaluates to TRUE when the most recent write to the export migration file completed successfully. The program uses this as a gate check after every record write — if this condition is not true, the export is aborted immediately to protect the integrity of the migration.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-CONTROL
variables.description: A grouped control area that holds the operational metadata governing the entire export run: the date and time the export was executed, the formatted timestamp applied to every exported record, and the running sequence counter that uniquely numbers each record. Together these fields provide the audit trail and ordering mechanism that the receiving branch system relies on for reconciliation.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-DATE
variables.description: The calendar date on which the branch migration export was executed, formatted as a 10-character string (e.g., YYYY-MM-DD). This date is used as part of the timestamp stamped on every exported record, allowing the receiving branch to confirm that all records originate from the same export run date.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-TIME
variables.description: The wall-clock time at which the branch migration export was executed, formatted as an 8-character string (e.g., HH:MM:SS). Combined with the export date, this provides a precise point-in-time reference for the snapshot of data captured in the migration file.

variables.name: WS-FORMATTED-TIMESTAMP
variables.description: The fully assembled date-and-time stamp of the export run, formatted as a 26-character string and applied to every single record written to the migration file. This timestamp serves as the primary traceability marker, enabling the receiving branch system to confirm that all records belong to the same migration event and to detect any records that may have been inserted from a different run.

variables.name: WS-SEQUENCE-COUNTER
variables.description: A monotonically increasing global sequence number that is incremented by one and stamped onto every record written to the migration export file, regardless of record type. Starting at zero, this counter creates an unbroken ordered audit trail across all five entity types (customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, cards), allowing the receiving branch system to detect any gaps (missing records), duplicates, or ordering anomalies during the import process.

variables.name: WS-TIMESTAMP-FIELDS
variables.description: A grouped working-storage area that holds the raw date and time components retrieved from the system clock at the start of the export run. These individual components (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, hundredths) are assembled into the formatted timestamp that is stamped on every migration record, establishing the precise point-in-time of the data snapshot.

variables.name: WS-CURRENT-DATE
variables.description: The calendar date portion of the system clock reading taken at the start of the export run, broken into its year, month, and day components. These components are used to build the date portion of the migration timestamp that identifies when the branch data snapshot was taken.

variables.name: WS-CURR-YEAR
variables.description: The four-digit calendar year in which the branch migration export was executed (e.g., 2024). Used as part of constructing the export timestamp that is stamped on every migration record for traceability.

variables.name: WS-CURR-MONTH
variables.description: The two-digit calendar month in which the branch migration export was executed (01–12). Used as part of constructing the export timestamp to precisely identify the date of the migration data snapshot.

variables.name: WS-CURR-DAY
variables.description: The two-digit day of the month on which the branch migration export was executed (01–31). Used as part of constructing the export timestamp to precisely identify the calendar date of the migration data snapshot.

variables.name: WS-CURRENT-TIME
variables.description: The wall-clock time portion of the system clock reading taken at the start of the export run, broken into hour, minute, second, and hundredths-of-a-second components. These components are used to build the time portion of the migration timestamp, providing sub-second precision for the point-in-time identification of the data snapshot.

variables.name: WS-CURR-HOUR
variables.description: The two-digit hour (00–23) at which the branch migration export was initiated. Used as part of the export timestamp to provide a precise time-of-day reference for the migration data snapshot.

variables.name: WS-CURR-MINUTE
variables.description: The two-digit minute (00–59) within the hour at which the branch migration export was initiated. Used as part of the export timestamp to narrow down the exact time the migration snapshot was taken.

variables.name: WS-CURR-SECOND
variables.description: The two-digit second (00–59) within the minute at which the branch migration export was initiated. Used as part of the export timestamp to provide second-level precision for the migration data snapshot time.

variables.name: WS-CURR-HUNDREDTH
variables.description: The two-digit hundredths-of-a-second component of the system clock at the moment the branch migration export was initiated. Provides sub-second precision to the export timestamp, which is especially useful if multiple export runs are executed within the same second and need to be distinguished from one another.

variables.name: WS-EXPORT-STATISTICS
variables.description: A grouped area that accumulates the final record counts for each business entity type exported during the migration run, plus a grand total. These statistics are displayed at job completion and serve as the primary operational audit record that branch operations staff and the receiving system use to verify that the expected volume of customers, accounts, cards, cross-references, and transactions was successfully migrated.

variables.name: WS-CUSTOMER-RECORDS-EXPORTED
variables.description: The running count of customer demographic and identity records successfully written to the migration export file during this run. At job completion this figure is reported to operations staff and must reconcile against the count of customer records imported by the receiving branch system to confirm no customers were lost or duplicated during migration.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-RECORDS-EXPORTED
variables.description: The running count of credit card account records (balances, credit limits, status, dates) successfully written to the migration export file. This count is reported at job completion and must match the number of account records loaded by the receiving branch system to confirm complete and accurate account data migration.

variables.name: WS-XREF-RECORDS-EXPORTED
variables.description: The running count of card-to-customer-to-account cross-reference linkage records successfully written to the migration export file. These records are critical for the receiving system to correctly associate each physical card with its owning customer and account; this count must reconcile with the import count to ensure no linkage relationships were broken during migration.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-RECORDS-EXPORTED
variables.description: The running count of credit card transaction records (purchases, payments, cash advances, etc.) successfully written to the migration export file. This count is reported at job completion and must reconcile with the transaction import count at the receiving branch to confirm that the complete transaction history for all migrating accounts has been transferred without loss.

variables.name: WS-CARD-RECORDS-EXPORTED
variables.description: The running count of physical credit card records (card numbers, CVV codes, embossed names, expiry dates, active status) successfully written to the migration export file. This count must reconcile with the card import count at the receiving branch to confirm that every physical card associated with the migrating accounts has been transferred.

variables.name: WS-TOTAL-RECORDS-EXPORTED
variables.description: The cumulative grand total of all records written to the migration export file across all five entity types (customers, accounts, cross-references, transactions, and cards). This single figure should equal the final value of WS-SEQUENCE-COUNTER and must match the total record count reported by the receiving branch system's import job, serving as the top-level reconciliation control total for the entire branch migration event.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-PROCESSING
paragraphs.description: This is the master orchestration paragraph that drives the entire branch migration export run. It sequences every phase of the migration — from setup through data extraction of all five business domains to final reporting — ensuring a complete, ordered export of all customer, account, card, and transaction data into the migration file.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs all pre-processing setup required before the migration export can begin, capturing the exact date and time of the run and ensuring all source and destination files are ready for processing. It establishes the operational context for the entire migration job and provides an auditable start marker in the job log.

paragraphs.name: 1050-GENERATE-TIMESTAMP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the current system date and time at the moment the export job runs and assembles them into a standardised 26-character timestamp that will be stamped on every exported record, providing a precise audit trail for reconciliation between the sending and receiving systems.

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.description: This paragraph acts as the migration pre-flight gate: it attempts to open all five source data files and the export output file before any data movement begins, aborting the entire job immediately if any single file is unavailable. This enforces the business rule that a migration run must never proceed with incomplete source data, preventing partial or corrupt export files from reaching the destination branch platform.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXPORT-CUSTOMERS
paragraphs.description: Drives the sequential export of all customer demographic and identity records from the source customer file into the migration export file. It reads every customer in turn, converts each into a tagged export record, and reports the final count for audit reconciliation.

paragraphs.name: 2100-READ-CUSTOMER-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Reads the next customer demographic record from the customer source file in sequence. If the read fails for any reason other than reaching the end of the file, the program halts immediately to prevent a corrupt or incomplete migration export.

paragraphs.name: 2200-CREATE-CUSTOMER-EXP-REC
paragraphs.description: Constructs and writes a single customer export record to the migration file, packaging the customer's full demographic profile — including sensitive identity data — with branch, region, timestamp, and sequence metadata. This record will be consumed by the receiving branch platform to recreate the customer in the destination system.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXPORT-ACCOUNTS
paragraphs.description: Drives the sequential export of all credit card account records from the source account master file into the migration output file. It reads every account in turn, writing each one to the export file, then reports the final count of accounts exported for audit and reconciliation purposes.

paragraphs.name: 3100-READ-ACCOUNT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Reads the next credit card account record from the account source file during the migration export process. If the read operation fails for any reason other than reaching the end of the file, the program halts immediately to prevent a corrupt or incomplete migration output.

paragraphs.name: 3200-CREATE-ACCOUNT-EXP-REC
paragraphs.description: Constructs and writes a single account export record to the migration file, packaging all credit card account details — balances, limits, dates, and status — with migration routing metadata and a unique sequence number. This paragraph is called once per account read from the source file, forming the account-domain contribution to the consolidated migration output.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXPORT-XREFS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full sequential export of all card-to-account cross-reference records from the source system, writing each linkage record to the migration file and reporting the final count for audit reconciliation.

paragraphs.name: 4100-READ-XREF-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Reads the next card-to-account cross-reference record from the cross-reference source file during the migration export. If the read fails for any reason other than reaching the end of the file, the program halts immediately to prevent a corrupt or incomplete migration output.

paragraphs.name: 4200-CREATE-XREF-EXPORT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Constructs and writes a single cross-reference export record that links a physical card number to its associated customer and account, tagging it with branch, region, timestamp, and a unique sequence number for migration traceability. This paragraph is called once per cross-reference entry to ensure every card-to-customer-to-account relationship is captured in the migration file.

paragraphs.name: 5000-EXPORT-TRANSACTIONS
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the sequential export of all credit card transaction records from the source transaction file into the migration export file. It drives a read-process loop that continues until every transaction has been extracted and written, then reports the final transaction count for audit purposes.

paragraphs.name: 5100-READ-TRANSACTION-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Reads the next credit card transaction record from the source transaction file during the migration export process. If the read fails for any reason other than reaching the end of the file, the program halts immediately to prevent a corrupt or incomplete migration output.

paragraphs.name: 5200-CREATE-TRAN-EXP-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph constructs and writes a single transaction record to the migration export file, capturing the full details of a credit card transaction — including merchant, amount, and timestamps — tagged for the target branch and region. It also increments the running transaction and overall export counts to maintain an accurate audit trail of the migration run.

paragraphs.name: 5500-EXPORT-CARDS
paragraphs.description: Drives the sequential export of all physical credit card records from the card source file into the migration export file. This paragraph forms the final data domain pass in the migration run, ensuring every card associated with migrating accounts is captured in the output.

paragraphs.name: 5600-READ-CARD-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Reads the next physical credit card record from the card source file during the card export pass. If the read operation fails for any reason other than reaching the end of the file, the program halts immediately to prevent a corrupt or incomplete migration.

paragraphs.name: 5700-CREATE-CARD-EXPORT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Constructs and writes a single physical credit card record into the migration export file, tagging it with branch, region, and run-time metadata so the receiving system can identify and load it correctly. This paragraph also maintains running counts of exported card records for end-of-job reconciliation.

paragraphs.name: 6000-FINALIZE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph concludes the migration export run by safely closing all source and output files, then producing an operational audit summary that reports how many records of each business entity type were successfully exported. These counts serve as the primary reconciliation reference for the receiving branch system when the companion import process is executed.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable failures during the migration export run by immediately halting the program in an abnormal state, preventing any partial, corrupt, or incomplete migration file from being silently accepted by the receiving branch system.
